# Decision history — lege-ecosystem

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## lege-ecosystem.decision.top-level-application-license-agpl

### Revision 1 — License the top-level Lege applications under AGPL-3.0-only

`active` · `@lege-ecosystem.decision.top-level-application-license-agpl/1` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "LICENSE"`, `path "NOTICE"`, `path "README.md"`, `path "lege-android/**"`, `path "lege-misc/docs/licenses.html"`, `path "lege-process/**"`, `path "lege-viewer/**"` · topic `top-level-application-license`

The Lege top-level workspace and combined application products are licensed AGPL-3.0-only, authorizing direct linking to the AGPL-3.0-only DJVULibRust crate. The root and application package metadata and included license texts must say AGPL-3.0-only. Independently usable codec and third-party subtrees retain their explicit licenses: DJVULibRust remains AGPL-3.0-only, while jbig2enc-rust and jp2lam remain MIT OR Apache-2.0.

**Context.** The user selected the plan's recommended D1 outcome: everything is AGPL again at the top level. The former MIT application declaration existed to support the now-retired arms-length subprocess boundary.

**Consequences.** Lege may restore the in-process DJVULibRust API. Application crates that directly link lege-process, including lege-android, must not continue to claim MIT. Mixed-license subtrees and third-party notices remain explicitly mapped rather than being relabeled.

## lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer.final-buffer-ownership

### Revision 1 — Allocate renderer and JPEG final buffers in their shared Arc layout

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer.final-buffer-ownership/1` · scope `path "lege-pdf/render/crates/pdf-image/src/jpeg/**"`, `path "lege-pdf/render/crates/pdf-render-cpu/**"` · topic `final-buffer-ownership`

Allocate CPU page surfaces and JPEG decoded output directly as uniquely-owned Arc slices, mutate them only while unique, and hand the Arc to HostPage or DecodedImage without a whole-buffer Vec-to-Arc conversion. Preserve Surface clone value semantics by deep-copying knockout-group snapshots.

## lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer.gray8-draws-take-the-rgb8-fast-paths

### Revision 1 — Gray8 image draws take the axis-aligned RGB8 fast paths through a one-time promotion; non-JPX decodes are cached without a target size

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer.gray8-draws-take-the-rgb8-fast-paths/1` · scope `path "lege-pdf/read/src/session.rs"`, `path "lege-pdf/render/crates/pdf-render-cpu/**"`

In `paint_image`, an opaque, normal-blend, unclipped, axis-aligned 8-bit gray image with no `/Decode` is re-expressed once as RGB8 (`PreparedImage::gray8_promoted_to_rgb8`: each byte tripled, colour space marked RGB, everything else cloned) before the fast-path eligibility tests, so the nearest, bilinear, area-minified and masked area-minified RGB8 painters apply to it. `pixel()` answers `[g, g, g, 255]` for such a gray texel and `[r, g, b, 255]` for RGB8, so the promoted draw is byte-identical by construction (test `gray8_draws_match_their_rgb8_twins`). A magnified draw under a mask has no fast path either way and is not expanded. Separately, `ImageCacheKey` keeps the target size only for JPX, the one codec that decodes at a reduced resolution; JBIG2, DCT and CCITT payloads are the same whatever the draw size, so a page rendered at two sizes decodes them once.

**Context.** The existing fast paths (@lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer.mrc-masked-draw-fast-path) accepted only RGB8 and CMYK sources. Scanned books and Lege's own MRC output are 8-bit DeviceGray almost without exception, so every page draw of Lege's main workload was taking the generic per-pixel sampler at roughly 250 ns per destination pixel: 1.0 s for a 1697x2400 page, 0.4 s at 1200 px, and the analysis render on top. Lege renders each page twice (bounded analysis render, then the output render), and the JBIG2 mask was decoded for both because the cache key carried the target size.

**Consequences.** Gobineau (MRC source: gray JPX foreground and background, JBIG2 SMask), 20 pages, per-stage CPU: output render 22.7 s -> 3.0 s at 2400 px and 8.1 s -> 1.7 s at 1200 px; analysis render 6.2 s -> 2.3 s; the shared image cache went from 0 hits to one hit per page. The JBIG2-mode output was byte-identical before the coverage-plane change that followed. The promotion costs one 3x copy of the source per draw (a 6 Mpx page: about 5 ms and 18 MiB transient), capped at 64 Mpx like the CMYK conversion.

## lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer.mrc-masked-draw-fast-path

### Revision 1 — MRC pages are shading-bound, not decode-bound: masked area-min fast path in pdf-render-cpu

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer.mrc-masked-draw-fast-path/1` · scope `path "lege-pdf/render/crates/pdf-render-cpu/**"`

Add `paint_axis_aligned_rgb8_area_min_masked` to `pdf-render-cpu/src/exec.rs`: an axis-aligned area-minification fast path for RGB8 image draws carrying a bilevel cut-out, covering both MRC mask encodings (1-bit `/SMask` coverage layer, and hard `/Mask` over an `/ImageMask` stencil). Per-column and per-row preparation of the inverse map, the base box-filter taps, and the mask's per-axis lookup replaces per-pixel recomputation. Byte-identical to the generic path, edge anti-aliasing included. Measured 2026-08-08; full record in lege-pdf/render/docs/refinement/performance-history/optimization-mrc-mask-20260808.md
